narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 63.3% chance that you would fail the bar exam on the first attempt. In practical terms, that is a majority-failure risk, so the decision treated your profile as not yet showing enough readiness for admission.

The most influential factor was your third-year class-rank decile. You are in the lowest decile, while admitted students averaged around the sixth decile; this placed you far below the typical admitted student and pushed the prediction most strongly toward failure. The second factor was your first-year class-rank decile. You were again in the lowest decile, against an admitted average near the sixth decile, so it also pushed toward failure. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.10 was the third factor. It is slightly below the admitted average of 3.23, but in the context of your overall profile it actually pushed modestly toward passing, meaning it softened the risk rather than caused the denial.

To improve a future application, focus on raising your academic standing in later law-school work and documenting any improvement in class rank. Also build a structured bar-exam readiness plan with diagnostics and targeted study. Gender and race were not used in this prediction.
